Assignment \(z\) reveals exactly the restriction \(\theta|_{O_z}\) on an observed coordinate set \(O_z\subseteq I\) and produces the linear score \(X_z(\theta)=v_z^\top\theta\) for a known coefficient vector \(v_z\in\mathbb R^K\). The assignment is the only source of randomness: the schedule is fixed and is not drawn from a superpopulation. The design mean score coefficient is \(c=\sum_zp_zv_z\), the target is \(\tau(\theta)=c^\top\theta\), the variance matrix is \(A=\sum_zp_zv_zv_z^\top-cc^\top\), and the true randomization variance is \(f(\theta)=\theta^\top A\theta=\operatorname{Var}_p\{X_z(\theta)\}\).
